limitations: No connected live user browser was available; deployed SNES runtime bytes matched the original checkout baseline. No live latency measurement or deployment was performed.

The broader Contra/WebKit loopback case timed out waiting for normal audio after player join in the candidate. The unchanged baseline also timed out at the same audio readiness check, for its viewer. These failures occurred at different stages and do not establish equivalence or exclude a regression for slower NES clients.
The first background-browser test attempt also suppressed Playwright RAF-based polling. Fixed its hidden-period waits to use timed polling; the corrected two-SNES run passed.
A browser/OS can still throttle or suspend a background page. The checks cover application-controlled pause, bounded display buffers, and timer-driven simulation, not suspended process execution.
